baseline.failure_type: Non-GAAP footnoted sub-row reported as total R&D; unit conversion slipped past verifier
baseline.root_cause: The generator picked the first R&D row, 'Research and development(1) | $ 6,690', instead of the 'Total expenses | $ 8,915' row of the same table, even though the table visibly decomposes 6,690 + 2,225 SBC = 8,915. The chunker split table c112 from its '(1) Excluding stock-based compensation' footnote (c113), so the qualifier was not attached to the row. The generator also converted 6,690 million to '$6.690 billion', a calculated value GENERATOR_SYSTEM forbids. The semantic verifier marked the claim supported ('$6,690 million, which equals $6.690 billion'), although VERIFIER_SYSTEM tells it to check 'GAAP/non-GAAP basis ... table headers and footnote qualifications'. The reranker also dropped all three p68 income-statement chunks, which carry only the unambiguous GAAP row '| Research and development | 8,915 |'.
baseline.evidence: Generator quote E46 = 'Research and development(1) |  | $ | 6,690 ...' (row index 3 of p52:table2). The same chunk contains '| Stock-based compensa on | 2,225 |' and '| Total expenses | $ 8,915 |'. Source document p68 has '| Research and development | | | 8,915 |'. The offline rebuild shows c113 begins '(1)\n\nExcluding stock-based compensation'. The verifier reason accepts the billion conversion. Gate max 1.177, so diagnostic_gate_6.359375_accepts=false: the calibrated gate would have correctly blocked this wrong answer.
baseline.suggested_mitigation: (1) In report_chunker, keep a table's trailing footnote lines ('(n) ...') in the same chunk or table_context unit. In source binding, attach the footnote text to any row whose label carries the matching '(n)' marker. Make validate_draft reject claims that cite a marker-bearing row unless the claim text carries the qualifier. (2) Add a deterministic check in validate_draft that every numeric token in the claim text appears verbatim in a cited quote; this rejects '6.690 billion' derived from '6,690'. (3) Add a GENERATOR_SYSTEM rule to prefer 'Total' rows and GAAP statement rows for spend/expense questions. (4) Reserve a top5 slot for, or set a reranker floor on, primary-statement chunks when the query names a line item.
baseline.verifier_notes: Outcome, stage and severity confirmed, and the gold is correct: p68 shows 8,915. I corrected the claim that 'the footnote chunk is at vector rank 14'. Rank 14 (c111) is the services-segment footnote. The R&D footnote lives in chunk c113, which is absent from the top20, because chunking separated it from table c112. That strengthens the chunker-level mitigation, which I added.

baseline.failure_type: Reranker dropped every dividends-per-share chunk; verifier also mis-rejected the correct EPS claim
baseline.root_cause: A correct answer needed the dividends-per-share row. All four top20 chunks with that row (FY2024 p43 at vector rank 4, FY2023 p43, FY2025 p44, FY2022 p43) scored below 2.77 and were cut, while three near-duplicate EPS-note tables and the letter prose took the slots. Without DPS values, the generator ignored its own 'abstain if any essential part is unsupported' rule and substituted a qualitative claim[1] ('raised its dividend in fiscal 2024', E5), which does not answer the FY2022-vs-FY2024 per-share movement. The verifier then made two errors. It rejected the correct claim[0] ('$4.42 in fiscal 2022 and decreased to $4.31 in fiscal 2024', E15 '$ 4.31 | $ 4.31 | $ 4.42') with an illogical reason: 'it did not decrease from 2022 to 2024 but decreased from 2022 to 2023 then remained flat'. Its rejection produced the abstention, but a correct verifier would have set answers_question=false and abstained too, so the error that decided the outcome was the reranker's exclusion of p43. The verifier's direction-logic error remains a latent defect: it could reject a correct answer even after p43 is retrieved.
baseline.evidence: Verifier claim_verdicts[0] supported=false with the reason quoted above; claim_verdicts[1] supported=true; answers_question=true. baseline.suggested_mitigation: Decompose multi-metric questions (diluted EPS + dividends per share) into per-metric sub-queries, each with its own reranked slots, or de-duplicate near-identical same-table chunks across report years before taking the top5, so the Statements of Earnings chunk is kept. Make the generator abstain, or name the missing metric, rather than give a qualitative substitute. For direction claims (increased/decreased) between quoted values, add a deterministic post-verifier check that parses the quoted endpoint values and confirms the sign; let it override, or trigger one retry of, a verifier rejection whose reason contradicts the arithmetic. Make answers_question require numeric evidence for every requested metric.

baseline.failure_type: Wrong fiscal year drafted plus NUL-for-NBSP quote corruption
baseline.root_cause: There were two compounding faults. (1) Generation, the stage that ruled out a correct answer: 'most recent annual report' was not resolved. The generator drafted the FY2022 paragraph ($30.4B at Dec 31, 2022; $5.5B not expected to be filled in 2023), citing E5 from the reranker-top1 CAT_FY2022 chunk. It ignored E35 (CAT_FY2025, $51.2B), even though each chunk in the bundle carries fiscal_year. (2) Reference validation, which triggered the abstention. The source E5 has U+00A0 in 'December 31, 2021', but the generator's JSON quote contained U+0000 at that spot. validate_draft runs _text() on the quote, and _text() rejects any Unicode category-C character other than \n\r\t (answer_verification.py, the _text check just before line 161). U+0000 is category Cc, so the quote failed with invalid_quote before the exact-substring check ran. That substring check would have returned quote_not_in_source instead. Apart from the NUL, the quote was verbatim: replacing it with U+00A0 makes it an exact substring of E5. A correctly reproduced NBSP (category Zs) would have passed. This failure was an accidental safety net. Had the quote passed, a wrong-year FY2022 answer would have gone to the verifier, and in D12 the same verifier approved a stale-year answer. E35 also contains U+00A0 ('December 31, 2024'), so even a correct full-paragraph quote was exposed to the same corruption. The calibrated diagnostic gate would also have refused (max 3.47 < 6.359), despite gold evidence in top5.

Tell the generator to use only evidence whose fiscal_year matches the resolved period and to state that period. Add a verifier check that rejects claims from an older report when a newer one for the same topic is in context. (b) Stop the model from having to echo invisible spacing. Map U+00A0/U+202F/U+2009 to ASCII space in the model-facing evidence text, keep an offset map back to the original source, and validate quotes against the normalised text while still resolving to exact source offsets. As a narrower fallback in validate_draft, before the _text() control-character guard, try replacing each U+0000 in a quote with the whitespace character found at the matching position of a source substring. Accept the quote only if it then matches exactly, and keep rejecting all other control characters.

baseline.failure_type: Evidence payload overflow from fragmented atoms
baseline.root_cause: The pipeline abstained before the generator call, at the check in generation.py line 157 (len(serialized) > max_context_chars). The limit is the default 100,000 because DemoService.answer does not pass max_context_chars. I rebuilt the bundle offline for the same five chunk_ids; the rebuild matches logged sizes for D10, D12 and D13 to the character. It has 178 evidence atoms with a median text length of 8 chars, and 119 atoms are 10 chars or fewer. These are layout-fragmented chart labels and MD&A table cells ('48.0', '%', '$', '2,575', '-24 %') bound as separate prose units. Each carries a roughly 700-char JSON envelope (citation sha256, source_file, document_id, pdf_page, locator, chunk_ids), and each atom's text is repeated again in chunks[].references. The evidence JSON came to 104,548 chars for only 9,229 chars of source text, and the serialized context to 135,118 chars. D13, for comparison, has 37 atoms and 63,826 chars. A secondary issue would have remained even within budget: top5 lacked the total-revenue refutation (p32 just missed at rerank 7; p35 ranked 20th). The generator would then likely have abstained, or risked a sycophantic 'reasons' answer built from the FY2025 decline text, and the prompt has no instruction to correct false premises. Keep sha256, source_file, locator and chunk_ids in an application-side registry keyed by evidence_id, and send only {evidence_id, text, ticker, fiscal_year, pdf_page}. Stop duplicating atom text inside chunks[].references. Coalesce consecutive tiny prose atoms from the same page or region into one line-group unit before binding. (2) On overflow, drop the lowest-reranked chunk(s) and retry instead of abstaining. (3) For questions that assert a magnitude or direction ('fall 30%'), run a premise-check retrieval with the assertion stripped (e.g. 'Nike fiscal 2023 total revenues') and force the headline revenue chunk (p32/p35) into context.
